answers.how: Depth-compensating the boat's motion from 0 to 1 s gives approximately 98.6 px/m at t=0. Its projected length is about 135 px.
The boat's shorter crosswise extent is approximately 40 px; dividing by the motion-calibrated scale of 98.6 px/m gives its width.
The hull's rim-to-bottom height is approximately 28 px, converted using the boat's calibrated scale.
The pier's short edge measures approximately 22 px. Correcting the boat-derived scale to the pier's 18.920 m depth gives about 61.6 px/m.
The shore-to-water-end extent is approximately 205 px, divided by the depth-corrected pier scale of 61.6 px/m.
Extrapolated the boat's trajectory to 3 s, giving a depth near 15.81 m, then compared the nearest hull point with the pier's outer end in depth-corrected coordinates.
The tread width is approximately 42 px. At the stairs' 23.125 m depth, the calibrated scale is approximately 50.4 px/m.
Measured approximately 28 px vertically from the pier deck to the waterline and applied the pier's depth-corrected scale.
Measured approximately 20 px vertically between the cabin floor and the ground, using the stairs' depth as the local depth reference.
